gloss: to awaken; to become alert; to be aroused

definitions.gloss: to awaken; to wake up; to become alert
definitions.explanation: To wake from sleep or become sharply alert and aware. Also used figuratively for becoming aware of a truth or reality.

definitions.gloss: to awaken to a talent or power; to be aroused
definitions.explanation: To discover or activate a hidden ability, potential, or awareness. Common in fiction and self-improvement contexts.

examples.japanese: コーヒーで{覚醒|かくせい}する。
{意識|いしき}が{覚醒|かくせい}した。
{麻酔|ますい}から{覚醒|かくせい}するまで{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: It took time to wake up from the anesthesia.

examples.japanese: {才能|さいのう}が{覚醒|かくせい}した。
{危機|きき}に{直面|ちょくめん}して、リーダーとしての{資質|ししつ}が{覚醒|かくせい}した。
examples.english: Facing a crisis, their leadership qualities were awakened.

examples.japanese: {主人公|しゅじんこう}が{隠|かく}された{力|ちから}に{覚醒|かくせい}する{場面|ばめん}が{一番|いちばん}{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: My favorite scene is when the protagonist awakens to their hidden power.

notes: A suru verb ({覚醒|かくせい}しない / {覚醒|かくせい}します / {覚醒|かくせい}して). Related compound: {覚醒剤|かくせいざい} (stimulant drug, amphetamine — a controlled substance in Japan). In medical contexts, {覚醒|かくせい} refers to a patient regaining consciousness. In anime and manga, {覚醒|かくせい} is a popular trope where a character unlocks hidden abilities. Different from {目覚|めざ}める, which is the everyday word for waking up from sleep.
